body.translated_text: The <s>Kośāmbakavastu</s> (Chapter on the Kośāmbī Affair)

children.translated_text: In the <s>Kośāmbakavastu</s>
Summary verse (<s>uddāna</s>):
The quarrel of the <s>Kośāmbaka</s> [monks], and the diverse disputes among the <s>bhikṣus</s>,
the wandering of <s>Dīrghika</s> while those [monks] were contending about the recitation,
and <s>Bhṛgu</s> in the salt-house, protected by the forest-grove elephant,
and <s>Aniruddha</s> — having done [all] this, [the Buddha] brings peace at <s>Śrāvastī</s>.

body.text: buddho bhagavān kośāmbyāṃ viharati ghoṣilārāme / tena khalu samayena kośāmbako bhikṣur vyāḍo vikrāntaḥ sūtradharo vinayadharo mātṛkādharaḥ / bahavaś cāsya bhikṣavaḥ sahāyakā vyāḍā vikrāntāḥ sūtradharā vinayadharā mātṛkādharāḥ / vaiśālyāṃ vaiśālako bhikṣur vyāḍo vikrāntaḥ sūtradharo vinayadharo mātṛkādharaḥ / bahavaś cāsya bhikṣavaḥ sahāyakā vyāḍā vikrāntāḥ sūtradharā vinayadharā mātṛkādharāḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Kośāmbī</s> in <s>Ghoṣilārāma</s>. At that time, there was a <s>bhikṣu</s> of <s>Kośāmbī</s> — bold, courageous, a master of the <s>Sūtra</s>, a master of the <s>Vinaya</s>, a master of the <s>Mātṛkā</s>. And many <s>bhikṣus</s> were his companions — bold, courageous, masters of the <s>Sūtra</s>, masters of the <s>Vinaya</s>, masters of the <s>Mātṛkā</s>. At <s>Vaiśālī</s>, there was a <s>bhikṣu</s> of <s>Vaiśālī</s> — bold, courageous, a master of the <s>Sūtra</s>, a master of the <s>Vinaya</s>, a master of the <s>Mātṛkā</s>. And many <s>bhikṣus</s> were his companions — bold, courageous, masters of the <s>Sūtra</s>, masters of the <s>Vinaya</s>, masters of the <s>Mātṛkā</s>.

body.text: atha vaiśālako bhikṣur apareṇa samayena janapadacārikāṃ caran kośāmbīm anuprāptaḥ / sa mārgaśramaṃ prativinodya kośāmbakasya bhikṣoḥ sakāśam upasaṃkrāntaḥ / upasaṃkramya parasparaṃ prativinodya sūtravinayābhir dharmeṣu viniścayaṃ kartum ārabdhau / tatraikaḥ kathayati / evam etat sūtraṃ paṭhitavyam* / ayam asya sūtrasyārthaḥ dvitīyaḥ kathayati (

children.translated_text: [MSV II 174]

children.text: ) / nedaṃ sūtram evaṃ paṭhitavyam* / nāsya sūtrasyāyam arthaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This <s>sūtra</s> should not be recited thus; this is not the meaning of this <s>sūtra</s>.'
'Yours [is wrong]' —

children.text: ayuktam* mama yuktam* / tava sahitam* / mamāsahitam* / taveti / tatas tayoḥ parasparaṃ vairuddhyam utpannam* / kośāmbako bhikṣur vaiśālakasya randhrānveṣaṇatatparas tiṣṭhate /
children.translated_text: 'Yours is unfitting, mine is fitting; yours is inconsistent, mine is consistent' — and so on. Thus, mutual hostility arose between them. The <s>Kośāmbaka bhikṣu</s> stood intent on seeking faults in the <s>Vaiśālaka</s>.

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Vaiśālaka bhikṣu</s>, at another time, while wandering on a tour of the countryside, arrived at <s>Kośāmbī</s>. Having dispelled the fatigue of the journey, he approached the <s>Kośāmbaka bhikṣu</s>. Having approached and exchanged mutual pleasantries, the two began to settle doctrinal points through the <s>Sūtra</s> and <s>Vinaya</s> teachings. There, one said: 'This <s>sūtra</s> should be recited thus; this is the meaning of this <s>sūtra</s>.' The second said:

body.text: saṃghena cāyam evaṃrūpaḥ kriyākāraḥ kṛtaḥ / yaḥ paśyed varcaskumbhikāṃ riktāṃ tucchāṃ nirudakāṃ tenodakasya pūrayitvā yathāsthāne sthā

children.translated_text: [and]

children.text: tavyā upadhivārikasya vārocayitavyā / varcaskumbhikā riktā tiṣṭhatīti / na ced ātmanā pūrayati nāpy upadhivārikasyārocayati tasyānādaro bhavati / anādarāc ca taṃ vayaṃ pāyantikām āpattiṃ deśayiṣyāma iti /
children.translated_text: should inform the provisions-keeper: "The excrement-pot stands empty." If he does not fill it himself nor inform the provisions-keeper, that constitutes a disregard. And because of disregard, we shall have him confess a <s>pāyantikā</s> (expiatory) offense.'

body.translated_text: Now, the <s>saṃgha</s> had made a procedural rule of this sort: 'Whoever sees the excrement-pot empty, hollow, and without water, he should fill it with water and place it in its proper spot,

body.text: yāvad anyatamena gṛhapatinā buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃgho 'ntargṛhe bhaktenopanimantritaḥ / tatra kecid bhikṣavo bhoktuṃ gatāḥ / kecid gantukāmāḥ / vaiśālakas tu bhikṣur varcaskumbhikām ādāya varcaskuṭiṃ praviṣṭaḥ / tasya sārdhaṃvihāro tvaritagatipracāratayā śabdayituṃ gataḥ / upādhyāya kecid bhikṣavo bhoktuṃ gatāḥ kecid gantukāmāḥ / āgacchata gacchāma iti / sa tena sārdhaṃ varcaskumbhikām ekasmin sthāne sthāpayitvā saṃprasthitaḥ / sa ca kośāmbako bhikṣus tam pradeśam anuprāptaḥ / tato 'sau vaiśālako bhikṣuḥ purastād varcaskumbhikāṃ gṛhītvā vihāraṃ praveṣṭum ārabdhaḥ / sārdhaṃvihāriṇā ucyate / (

children.translated_text: [MSV II 175]

children.text: ) upādhyāya kiṃ bhūyaḥ praviśasi / sa kathayati / putra mamāyaṃ kośāmbako bhikṣur avatāraprekṣī / varcaskumbhikāṃ pūrayituṃ praviśāmi / kim ayaṃ sarveṇa sarvaṃ riktā / na sarveṇa sarvam* / api tu na labhyam anenodakenodakakṛtyaṃ kartum* / upādhyāya kevalaṃ sarveṇa sarvaṃ riktā bhavatu / vayam upādhyāyasya pakṣo balaṃ sahāyakāḥ / āgacchata / gacchāmaḥ / sa tāṃ tatraiva sthāpayitvā tena sārdhaṃ gataḥ / kośāmbakena bhikṣuṇā dṛṣṭā sā ca kumbhikā parāmṛṣṭā / tataḥ saṃjātāmarṣo hum iti kṛtvā varcaskumbhikāṃ (
children.translated_text: 'Preceptor, why are you entering again?' He said: 'Son, this <s>Kośāmbaka bhikṣu</s> of mine is looking for an opportunity [to find fault]. I am entering to fill the excrement-pot.' 'Is it entirely empty?' 'Not entirely. But it is not possible for him to use that water for the water-task.' 'Preceptor, let it simply be entirely empty. We are the preceptor's party, strength, and allies. Come, let us go.' He, having placed it right there, went with him. The <s>Kośāmbaka bhikṣu</s> saw it and examined the pot. Then, anger having arisen, with a 'humph!' [he noted it]. Having [later]

children.text: ) pūrayitvā udakakāryaṃ kṛtvā gataḥ / tato bhukte bhikṣusaṃghe vihāram āgate bhikṣūn pracārayitum ārabdhaḥ / āyuṣmantaḥ anena bhikṣuṇā vaiśālakena saṃghasya kriyākāro bhagna iti / tato yathāvṛddhikayā sāmīciṃ kurvāṇo 'nupūrveṇa tasya sakāśam upasaṃkrāntaḥ / kathayati / āyuṣman avakāśaṃ kuru / kṛto bhavatu / āpattir asyāpannā / yathādharmaṃ kuru / na paśyāmy āpattim* / nanu saṃghena kriyākāraḥ kṛto yaḥ paśyed varcaskumbhikāṃ riktāṃ tucchāṃ nirudakāṃ tenātmanā udakasya pūrayitvā yathāsthāne sthāpayitavyā / upadhivārikasya vārocayitavyā / āyuṣman varcaskumbhikā riktā tiṣṭhatīti / na ced ātmanā pūrayati / nāpy upadhivārikasyārocayati / tasyānādaro bhavati / anādarāc ca taṃ vayaṃ pāyantikām āpattiṃ deśayiṣyāma iti / sa kathayati / na (
children.translated_text: filled the excrement-pot, performed the water-duty, and gone. Then, after the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> had eaten and returned to the <s>vihāra</s>, he began to accuse [the Vaiśālaka] before the <s>bhikṣus</s>: 'Venerable ones, this <s>bhikṣu</s>, the <s>Vaiśālaka</s>, has broken the procedural rule of the <s>saṃgha</s>!' Then, approaching [the Vaiśālaka] in order of seniority while performing the proper salutations, he said: 'Venerable one, make room [for discussion].' 'Let it be done.' 'An offense has been committed by you. Act according to the <s>dharma</s>.' 'I do not see an offense.' 'But has not the <s>saṃgha</s> made a procedural rule: whoever sees the excrement-pot empty, hollow, and without water, he should fill it with water himself and place it in its proper spot; should inform the provisions-keeper: "Venerable one, the excrement-pot stands empty." If he does not fill it himself, nor inform the provisions-keeper, that constitutes a disregard. And because of disregard, we shall have him confess a <s>pāyantikā</s> offense.' He said: 'It was not
[MSV II 176]

children.text: ) sā riktā / mā bhavatu riktā / na labhyaṃ tenodakenodakakāryaṃ kartum* / sa tūṣṇīm avasthitaḥ /
children.translated_text: empty.' 'Let it not have been empty. It was not possible to perform the water-task with that water.' He remained silent.

body.translated_text: Then a certain householder had invited the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s> for a meal inside his house. Some <s>bhikṣus</s> had gone to eat; some wished to go. But the <s>Vaiśālaka bhikṣu</s>, having taken the excrement-pot, entered the latrine. His co-resident, proceeding with haste, went to call him: 'Preceptor, some <s>bhikṣus</s> have gone to eat, some wish to go. Come, let us go.' He, together with him, placed the excrement-pot in one spot and set out. And that <s>Kośāmbaka bhikṣu</s> arrived at that spot. Then the <s>Vaiśālaka bhikṣu</s>, having taken the excrement-pot from in front, began to enter the <s>vihāra</s>. His co-resident said:

body.text: kośāmbako bhikṣuḥ kośāmbyāṃ naivāsiko bahuparivāraś ca / tena tasya balād utkṣepaṇīyaṃ karma kṛtam iti / vaiśālakā bhikṣavaḥ kṣubdhā iti / tatra kośāmbakānāṃ vaiśālakānāṃ ca bhikṣūṇām utpannaḥ kalaho bhaṇḍanaṃ vigraho vivādo yaduta āpanna iti vā anāpanna iti vā / yat punar āpanno nānāpannaḥ / utkṣipto nānutkṣiptakaḥ / yat punar utkṣiptaḥ adharmeṇa karmaṇā kopyena sthāpanārheṇeti / etat prakaraṇaṃ bhikṣavo bhagavata ārocayanti / tato bhagavān utkṣiptakaṃ bhikṣum utkṣiptakānuvartakaṃ bhikṣum utkṣiptakānuvartakā

If I do not acknowledge my offense according to the <s>dharma</s>,
[MSV II 177]

children.translated_text: the <s>saṃgha</s> would dwell in quarrel, born of dispute, in conflict, fallen into contention. Therefore, let me acknowledge my offense according to the <s>dharma</s>." If the suspended <s>bhikṣu</s> does not undertake the prescribed rules of proper conduct, he commits a transgression (<s>sātisāra</s>).'

body.translated_text: The <s>Kośāmbaka bhikṣu</s>, being a resident of <s>Kośāmbī</s> with a large retinue, forcibly performed the act of suspension (<s>utkṣepaṇīya karma</s>) against him. The <s>Vaiśālaka bhikṣus</s> were agitated. Thus, among the <s>Kośāmbaka</s> and <s>Vaiśālaka bhikṣus</s>, there arose quarrel, dispute, conflict, and contention — namely: 'He has committed an offense' or 'He has not committed an offense.' Moreover, 'He has offended, he has not not-offended; he is suspended, he is not un-suspended.' Furthermore, 'He who is suspended [was suspended] by an unlawful act, objectionable, deserving of reversal.' The <s>bhikṣus</s> reported this matter to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having summoned through a messenger the suspended <s>bhikṣu</s>, the <s>bhikṣus</s> who followed the suspended one, and those who followed the followers of the suspended one,

body.text: atha bhagavān utkṣiptakaṃ bhikṣum utkṣiptakānuvartakān bhikṣūn utkṣiptakānuvartakānuvartakāṃś codyojya utkṣepakaṃ bhikṣum utkṣepakānuvartakān bhikṣūn utkṣepakānuvartakānuvartakāṃś ca dūtena prakrośyedam avocat* / satyaṃ yuṣmākaṃ bhikṣava utpannaḥ kalaho bhaṇḍanaṃ vigraho vivādo yadutāpanna iti vā pūrvavad yāvat sthāpanārheṇeti / satyaṃ bhadanta / mā bhikṣavaḥ kalaho mā bhaṇḍanaṃ mā vigraho mā vivādaḥ / api tūtkṣepakasyāhaṃ bhikṣor āsamudācārikān dharmān prajñapayiṣyāmi / utkṣepakeṇa bhikṣuṇā evaṃ cittam utpādayitavyam* / ayam utkṣiptako bhikṣur vyāḍo vikrāntaḥ sūtradharo (

Even now, on the <s>poṣadha</s> (observance) day, they bring about non-observance. The monks reported this matter to the Blessed One.

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having exhorted the suspended <s>bhikṣu</s>, the <s>bhikṣus</s> who followed the suspended one, and those who followed the followers of the suspended one, summoned through a messenger the suspending <s>bhikṣu</s>, the <s>bhikṣus</s> who followed the suspender, and those who followed the followers of the suspender, and spoke thus: 'Is it true that among you <s>bhikṣus</s> there has arisen quarrel, dispute, conflict, and contention — namely, "He has committed an offense," as before, up to "deserving of reversal"?' 'It is true, <s>Bhadanta</s>.' 'Let there be no quarrel among you <s>bhikṣus</s>, no dispute, no conflict, no contention. Furthermore, I shall prescribe rules of proper conduct for the suspending <s>bhikṣu</s>. The suspending <s>bhikṣu</s> should generate this thought: "This suspended <s>bhikṣu</s> is bold, courageous, a master of the <s>Sūtra</s>,

body.text: atha bhagavān utkṣiptakaṃ bhikṣum utkṣiptakānuvartakāṃś ca bhikṣūn utkṣiptakānuvartakānuvartakāṃś ca dūtena prakrośyedam avocat* / satyaṃ yūyaṃ bhikṣava evam ucyamānā api mayā kalahajātā eva viharatha bhaṇḍanajātā vigṛhītā vivādam āpannāḥ / apīdānīṃ poṣadhe 'py apoṣadham āgamayatha / satyaṃ bhadanta / mā bhikṣavaḥ kalaho mā bhaṇḍanaṃ mā vigraho mā vivādaḥ / kalahajātānāṃ yuṣmākaṃ bhikṣavo viharatāṃ bhaṇḍanajātānāṃ vigṛhītānāṃ vivādam āpannānāṃ yāni karmāṇi kriyante Ō poṣadhaḥ pravāraṇā jñaptir jñaptidvitīyaṃ jñapticaturthaṃ karmaṃ Ō kṛtāny akṛtāni bhavanti kopyāni /
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having summoned by messenger the suspended monk, the monks who followed the suspended one, and the monks who followed the followers of the suspended one, said this: 'Is it true, monks, that even when spoken to by me in this way, you continue to dwell in quarrel, dispute, contention, and controversy? And that even now, on the <s>poṣadha</s> day, you bring about non-observance?' 'It is true, Venerable Sir.' 'Monks, let there be no quarrel, no dispute, no contention, no controversy! When you monks dwell in quarrel, dispute, contention, and controversy, whatever formal acts are performed — <s>poṣadha</s>, <s>pravāraṇā</s> (invitation ceremony), motions (<s>jñapti</s>), acts with a motion and a second proclamation (<s>jñaptidvitīya</s>), acts with a motion and a fourth proclamation (<s>jñapticaturtha</s>) — [such] acts, though performed, become as if not performed, and are subject to annulment.'

body.text: nānāsaṃvāsikā yūyaṃ bhikṣavas teṣāṃ bhikṣūṇām* / te ca yuṣmākam* / tat kasya hetoḥ / dvāv imau bhikṣavo nānāsaṃvāsikau / kaś caivātmani cātmānaṃ nānāsaṃvāsikaṃ sthāpayati / yo vā saṃghena dharmatayā sthāpyate / katham ātmanaivātmānaṃ nānāsaṃvāsikaṃ sthāpayati / yathāpi tad bhikṣubhir bhikṣūṇāṃ kalahajātānāṃ viharatāṃ bhaṇḍanajātānāṃ vigṛhītānāṃ vivādam āpannānāṃ pakṣāparapakṣavyavasthitānāṃ saṃcintya dharmapakṣād (

children.translated_text: MSV II 179

children.text: ) adharmapakṣaṃ saṃkrāmati evam ātmanaivātmānaṃ nānāsaṃvāsikaṃ sthāpayati / kathaṃ saṃghena sthāpyaḥ / yathāpi tat saṃghenātmanā
children.translated_text: cross over to the faction of non-<s>Dharma</s> — thus one places oneself as being of separate communion. How is one placed by the <s>Saṅgha</s>? When one is suspended by the <s>Saṅgha</s> itself
for non-

children.text: yotkṣipyate / apratikarmaṇi apratinisṛṣṭe pāpake dṛṣṭigate utkṣipyate / evaṃ saṃghena dharmatayā /

body.text: śṛṇotu bhadantaḥ saṃghaḥ / yan nidānam apy āyuṣmata utpannaḥ kalaho bhaṇḍanaṃ vigraho vivādaḥ pūrvavad

children.translated_text: up to —

children.text: / so 'yam evaṃnāmā utkṣiptako bhikṣuḥ saṃghād osāraṇaṃ yācate / tat saṃgha evaṃnāmānaṃ bhikṣum osārayati / yeṣām āyuṣmatāṃ kṣamante evaṃnāmānam utkṣiptakaṃ bhikṣum osārayitum* / te tūṣṇīm* / na kṣamante / bhāṣantām* / osāritaḥ saṃghena evaṃnāmā utkṣiptako bhikṣuḥ / kṣāntam anujñātaṃ saṃghena / yasmāt tūṣṇīm evam etad dhārayāmi /
children.translated_text: 'This monk named so-and-so, who was suspended, requests reinstatement (<s>osāraṇā</s>) from the <s>Saṅgha</s>. Let the <s>Saṅgha</s> reinstate the monk named so-and-so. Those venerable ones who approve of reinstating the suspended monk named so-and-so — let them remain silent. Those who do not approve — let them speak. The suspended monk named so-and-so has been reinstated by the <s>Saṅgha</s>. It is approved and consented to by the <s>Saṅgha</s>. Since [the assembly] is silent, I shall record it thus.'

body.translated_text: 'Let the venerable <s>saṃgha</s> hear! Because of the venerable one, there has arisen quarrel, dispute, conflict, and contention' — as before,

body.text: osāraṇīyaṃ karma / tasyāhaṃ bhikṣor āsamudācārikān dharmān prajñapayāmi / osāraṇīyakarmakṛtena bhikṣūṇā saṃghāt sāmagrī yācayitavyā / evaṃ ca punar yācayitavyā /
body.translated_text: The reinstatement act (<s>osāraṇīya karma</s>). I shall prescribe the rules of deportment for that monk. The monk for whom the reinstatement act has been performed should request reconciliation (<s>sāmagrī</s>) from the <s>Saṅgha</s>. And he should request it thus:

body.text: śṛṇotu bhadantaḥ saṃghaḥ / yan nidānaṃ mamotpannaḥ kalaho bhaṇḍanaṃ vigraho vivādo yadutāpanna iti vā anāpanna iti vā / utkṣipta iti vā anutkṣipta iti vā / so 'ham āpanno nānāpannaḥ / utkṣiptako nānutkṣiptakaḥ / yat punar utkṣipto dharmeṇa karmaṇā akopyenāsthāpanārheṇa / tena mayā evaṃnāmnā (

children.text: ) utkṣiptakena bhikṣuṇā saṃghād osāraṇā yācitā / kṛtaṃ mama saṃghenosāraṇīyaṃ karma / so 'ham evaṃnāmā osāraraṇīyakarmakṛto bhikṣusaṃghāt sāmagrīṃ yāce / dadātu bhadantaḥ saṃgho mamaivaṃnāmna osāritasya bhikṣoḥ saṃghasāmagrīm* / anukampayānukampām upādāya / evaṃ dvir api / evaṃ trir api / tataḥ paścād ekena bhikṣuṇā jñaptiṃ kṛtvā karma kartavyam* /
children.translated_text: 'the suspended monk, reinstatement has been requested from the <s>Saṅgha</s>. The <s>Saṅgha</s> has performed the reinstatement act for me. I, named so-and-so, the monk for whom the reinstatement act has been performed, request reconciliation from the community of monks. Let the venerable <s>Saṅgha</s> give reconciliation (<s>saṃghasāmagrī</s>) to me, the reinstated monk named so-and-so, out of compassion.' Thus a second time. Thus a third time. Thereafter, one monk, having made the motion (<s>jñapti</s>), should perform the act:

body.translated_text: 'Let the venerable <s>Saṅgha</s> hear me. Because of whatever quarrel, dispute, contention, and controversy arose concerning me — whether [I was declared] one who has committed an offense or one who has not, whether [I was declared] suspended or not suspended — I have indeed committed the offense and was not un-offending; I was indeed suspended and was not un-suspended. And I was suspended by a lawful act, irrevocable and not subject to reversal. By me, named so-and-so,'

body.text: śṛṇotu bhadanta saṃghaḥ / yan nidānam asyāyuṣmata utpannaḥ kalaho bhaṇḍanaṃ vigraho vivādo yadutāpanna iti pūrvavad

children.translated_text: up to:

children.text: / sacet saṃghasya prāptakālaṃ kṣametānujānīyāt saṃgho yat saṃgha evaṃnāmnaḥ osāraṇīyakarmakṛtasya bhikṣoḥ sāmagrīṃ dadyād iti / eṣā jñaptiḥ / karma kartavyam* /
children.translated_text: 'If the <s>Saṅgha</s> finds the time appropriate, may the <s>Saṅgha</s> approve and consent that the <s>Saṅgha</s> grant reconciliation to the monk named so-and-so for whom the reinstatement act has been performed. This is the motion. The act should be performed:'

body.translated_text: 'Let the venerable <s>Saṅgha</s> hear me. Because of whatever quarrel, dispute, contention, and controversy arose for this venerable one — whether [he was declared] one who committed an offense — as before

body.text: śṛṇotu bhadanta saṃghaḥ / yan nidānam asyāyuṣmata utpannaḥ kalaho bhaṇḍanaṃ vigraho vivādo yadutāpannaḥ pūrvavad yāvad dattā saṃghena evaṃnāmnaḥ osāraṇīyakarmakṛtasya bhikṣoḥ sāmagrī / kśāntam anujñātam* / yasmāt tūṣṇīm evam etad dhārayāmi / ity asya saṃghena osāraṇīyakarmakṛtasya bhikṣoḥ sāmagrī dattā bhavati / tasya saṃghena sāmagrī dātavyā / nātra kaukṛtyaṃ karaṇīyam* /
body.translated_text: 'Let the venerable <s>Saṅgha</s> hear me. Because of whatever quarrel, dispute, contention, and controversy arose for this venerable one — whether [he was declared] one who committed an offense — as before, up to: Reconciliation has been granted by the <s>Saṅgha</s> to the monk named so-and-so for whom the reinstatement act has been performed. It is approved and consented to. Since [the assembly] is silent, I shall record it thus.' Thus reconciliation is granted by the <s>Saṅgha</s> to the monk for whom the reinstatement act has been performed. Reconciliation should be granted to him by the <s>Saṅgha</s>. No remorse should be entertained in this matter.

body.text: saṃghasāmagrīdattakasyāhaṃ bhikṣor āsamudācārikān dharmān prajñapayāmi / saṃghasāmagrīdattakena bhikṣuṇā poṣadho yācitavyaḥ / evaṃ ca punar yācitavyaḥ / śayanāsanaprajñaptiṃ kṛtvā pūrvavad yāvat* / so 'ham evaṃnāmā saṃghasāmagrīdattakaḥ saṃghāt sāmagrīpoṣadhaṃ yāce / dadātu bhadantaḥ saṃghaḥ mamaivaṃnāmnaḥ sāmagrīdattakasya bhikṣoḥ sāmagrīpoṣadham anukampām upādāya / evaṃ dvir api / trir api / tataḥ paścād ekena bhikṣuṇā jñaptiṃ kṛtvā karma kartavyam* /
body.translated_text: I shall prescribe the rules of deportment for the monk to whom <s>Saṅgha</s>-reconciliation has been granted. The monk to whom <s>Saṅgha</s>-reconciliation has been granted should request the reconciliation-<s>poṣadha</s> (observance ceremony). And he should request it thus: Having arranged the sleeping quarters — as before, up to: 'I, named so-and-so, to whom <s>Saṅgha</s>-reconciliation has been granted, request from the <s>Saṅgha</s> the reconciliation-<s>poṣadha</s>. Let the venerable <s>Saṅgha</s> grant the reconciliation-<s>poṣadha</s> to me, the monk named so-and-so to whom reconciliation has been granted, out of compassion.' Thus a second time. A third time. Thereafter, one monk, having made the motion, should perform the act:

body.text: śṛṇotu bhadantaḥ saṃghaḥ / yan nidānam asyāyuṣmata utpannaḥ kalaho bhaṇḍanaṃ vigraho vivādo yadutāpanna iti vā pūrvavad yāvat* / so 'yam evaṃnāmā saṃghasāmagrīdattakaḥ saṃghāt sāmagrīpoṣadhaṃ yācate / sacet saṃghasya prāptakālaṃ kṣametānujānīyāt saṃgho yat saṃgha evaṃnāmnaḥ saṃghasāmagrīdattakasya bhikṣoḥ sāmagrīpoṣadhaṃ dadyād iti / eṣā jñaptiḥ / karma kartavyam* /
body.translated_text: 'Let the venerable <s>Saṅgha</s> hear me. Because of whatever quarrel, dispute, contention, and controversy arose for this venerable one — whether [he was declared] one who committed an offense — as before, up to: This monk named so-and-so, to whom <s>Saṅgha</s>-reconciliation has been granted, requests the reconciliation-<s>poṣadha</s> from the <s>Saṅgha</s>. If the <s>Saṅgha</s> finds the time appropriate, may the <s>Saṅgha</s> approve and consent that the <s>Saṅgha</s> grant the reconciliation-<s>poṣadha</s> to the monk named so-and-so to whom <s>Saṅgha</s>-reconciliation has been granted. This is the motion. The act should be performed:'

body.text: śṛṇotu bhadantaḥ saṃghaḥ / yan nidānam asyāyuṣmata utpannaḥ kalaho bhaṇḍanaṃ vigraho vivādo yadutāpanna iti vā anāpanna iti vā pūrvavad yāvat* / so 'yam evaṃnāmā sāmagrīdattakaḥ saṃghāt sāmagrīpoṣadhaṃ yācate / tat saṃgha evaṃnāmnaḥ sāmagrīdattakasya bhikṣoḥ sāmagrīpoṣadhaṃ dadāti / eṣām āyuṣmatāṃ kṣamante evaṃnāmnaḥ sāmagrīdattakasya bhikṣoḥ sāmagrīpoṣadhaṃ dātum* / te tūṣṇīm* / na kṣamante / bhāṣantām* / dattaḥ saṃghena evaṃnāmnaḥ sāmagrīdattakasya bhikṣoḥ sāmagrīpoṣadhaḥ / kṣāntam anujñātaṃ saṃghena / yasmāt tūṣṇīm evam etad dhārayāmi /
body.translated_text: 'Let the venerable <s>Saṅgha</s> hear me. Because of whatever quarrel, dispute, contention, and controversy arose for this venerable one — whether [he was declared] one who committed an offense, or one who had not — as before, up to: This monk named so-and-so, to whom reconciliation has been granted, requests the reconciliation-<s>poṣadha</s> from the <s>Saṅgha</s>. The <s>Saṅgha</s> hereby grants the reconciliation-<s>poṣadha</s> to the monk named so-and-so to whom reconciliation has been granted. Those venerable ones who approve of granting the reconciliation-<s>poṣadha</s> to the monk named so-and-so to whom reconciliation has been granted — let them remain silent. Those who do not approve — let them speak. The reconciliation-<s>poṣadha</s> has been granted by the <s>Saṅgha</s> to the monk named so-and-so to whom reconciliation has been granted. It is approved and consented to by the <s>Saṅgha</s>. Since [the assembly] is silent, I shall record it thus.'

body.text: yasya saṃghena sāmagrīdattakasya bhikṣoḥ sāmagrīpoṣadho datto bhavati tena sārdhaṃ saṃghenaikatye niṣadya poṣadhaḥ kartavyaḥ pravāraṇā jñaptiḥ jñaptidvitīyaṃ jñapticaturthaṃ karma / nātra kaukṛtyaṃ karaṇīyam* / vyagrāḥ kurvanti sātisārā bhavanti / na ca punar bhikṣuṇā apoṣadhe poṣadham āgamayati / sātisāro bhavati / sthāpayitvā maṅgalyapoṣadhaṃ sāmagrīpoṣadhaṃ vā /
body.translated_text: The monk to whom the <s>Saṅgha</s> has granted the reconciliation-<s>poṣadha</s> — together with him, the <s>Saṅgha</s>, sitting as one [assembly], should perform the <s>poṣadha</s>, <s>pravāraṇā</s> (invitation ceremony), motions (<s>jñapti</s>), acts with a motion and a second proclamation, and acts with a motion and a fourth proclamation. No remorse should be entertained in this matter. Those who perform [these acts] carelessly commit an offense. Moreover, a monk should not bring about non-observance during a [valid] <s>poṣadha</s>; [if he does,] he commits an offense — except for the auspicious <s>poṣadha</s> (<s>maṅgalyapoṣadha</s>) or the reconciliation-<s>poṣadha</s> (<s>sāmagrīpoṣadha</s>).

body.text: kośāmbakavastu samāptam* //
body.translated_text: The <s>Kośāmbakavastu</s> (Chapter on the Kośāmbī Incident) is completed.
